#!/usr/bin/env python3
import argparse
import sys


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Count lines, words, and characters in a file."
    )
    parser.add_argument("file", nargs="?", default=None, help="File to read (or - for stdin)")

    group = parser.add_mutually_exclusive_group()
    group.add_argument("-l", action="store_true", help="Count lines")
    group.add_argument("-w", action="store_true", help="Count words")
    group.add_argument("-c", action="store_true", help="Count characters")

    args = parser.parse_args()

    # Determine if any flags were given
    has_l = args.l
    has_w = args.w
    has_c = args.c

    # If no flags at all, show all three
    show_all = not (has_l or has_w or has_c)

    # Determine the file to read
    filename = args.file
    if filename is None or filename == "-":
        fh = sys.stdin.buffer  # read as bytes so character count = byte count
    else:
        fh = open(filename, "rb")

    try:
        data = fh.read()
    finally:
        if fh is not sys.stdin.buffer:
            fh.close()

    # Count characters (bytes)
    char_count = len(data)

    # Count lines: split on b'\n'; a final line without trailing newline still counts
    # e.g. b"abc\ndef\n" -> [b"abc", b"def", b""] => 2 lines
    #      b"abc\ndef"   -> [b"abc", b"def"]     => 2 lines
    if len(data) == 0:
        line_count = 0
    else:
        line_count = data.count(b"\n")

    # Count words
    word_count = len(data.split())

    # Build output in fixed order: lines, words, characters
    results = []
    if show_all or has_l:
        results.append(str(line_count))
    if show_all or has_w:
        results.append(str(word_count))
    if show_all or has_c:
        results.append(str(char_count))

    print(" ".join(results))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
